name: RACI vs. DACI Decision & Responsibility Allocation Matrices
diagnostic: Architectural paralysis where pull requests languish indefinitely awaiting sign-off; multi-party ownership where "everyone owns, hence nobody owns" critical service components; executive overrides late in deployment phases.

script.label: DACI Escalation
script.text: "This architectural initiative has halted due to diffuse decision rights. We are adopting a DACI framework for this deliverable. Contributor A is designated the Driver; Principal Engineer B is the sole Approver; domain specialists C and D are Contributors; the remaining squad members are Informed. The Driver coordinates input, and the Approver will deliver a binding technical decision by Thursday at 15:00 UTC."

audit: Did one named Approver sign off, without a second committee review?
Did uninformed stakeholders stay out of the release-blocking path?
auditFull: Were pull requests and architectural RFCs reviewed and signed off by the singular designated Approver without secondary committee reviews?
Did uninformed stakeholders refrain from blocking deployment pipelines during release testing?
foundation: Traced to organizational design matrices from Project Management Institute standards and Intuit’s adaptation of DACI (Driver, Approver, Contributor, Informed), these models mitigate bystander apathy (Darley & Latané, 1968) and structural ambiguity in decision-making.

origin.title: A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide)
